scenario: AITA for telling an intern to throw her banana peel in the trash? | A few details to set the stage: To get into my place of work, one needs to walk from the parking lot down a sidewalk that is along the side of the building. The other side of the sidewalk is semi-wooded with low growing evergreen shrubs. This sidewalk is about 100ft long, and has a trash can at either end. Also, in the last month, there have been a ton of flies buzzing around this area, so much so that the building manager called an exterminator. This morning, I (\~30s F) witnessed an intern (20s F) for one of the companies in our building walking into work eating a banana. About 3/4 of the way down the sidewalk, with a trashcan not even 25 feet away, she tossed the banana peel into the bushes. It landed on top of the bush and she just kept walking. I wasn't sufficiently caffeinated to be polite, so I blurted out "What the hell? There's a trash can right in front of you!" complete with the WTF hand gesture; pointing to the trash can. She ripped into me, claiming it's organic and feeds the animals. She was half yelling / half crying. I pointed at the peel sitting on top of the bush and told her to "pick up your (her) damn banana peel." Instead she cried loudly saying something unintelligible, got her peel, and put it in the trash. I'm thinking, great, this is over. Maybe she won't toss her banana debris into the bushes and we will have less flies. I'm sure I could have been more nice about it / sworn less, but I was just so shocked to see someone litter like that. I badged in to the building and she walked in behind me. At some point, she must have cried to her boss about it, because her boss found me today and asked if I confronted her intern. I said I had, then explained, as I have done here, about the banana peel. I guess she spent all morning crying about how "mean" I was and couldn't do any work. My brain was screaming "drama queen" but I apologized instead for upsetting the intern. We laughed together about absurdity of it all, especially over a banana peel! But now that it's the weekend and I'm sufficiently caffeinated, I'm wondering AITA for calling her out?

I mean, why would someone throw trash into bushes when there's a trash can right there? Plus, there had been a lot of flies around recently, which is probably why the building manager called an exterminator. So, throwing food waste into the bushes could be contributing to the fly problem. I blurted out, "What the hell? There's a trash can right in front of you!" and gestured with my hands. She got defensive, saying it's organic and feeds the animals. I pointed out the peel was sitting on top of the bush and told her to pick it up. Instead, she cried, got the peel, and threw it in the trash. I thought it was over, but apparently, she told her boss about it, and her boss confronted me. I apologized for upsetting her, and we laughed about how absurd the whole situation was, especially over a banana peel. But now, on the weekend, I'm wondering if I was right to call her out like that. So, was I right or wrong? Let's break it down. First, the intern was littering. There's a clear rule against littering, and there are trash cans available. So, from that perspective, she was doing something wrong. Throwing the peel into the bushes isn't just unsightly; it can attract pests like flies, which was already an issue in the area. On the other hand, she was an intern, probably new to the workplace, and maybe she didn't realize the impact of her actions. She thought it was organic and would feed the animals, which, in a way, is a positive intention, but it's not the right way to dispose of waste. I was upset because I saw her littering and wanted her to do the right thing. But the way I confronted her was pretty harsh. I wasn't calm or polite; I was shocked and maybe a bit rude. But now I'm reflecting on whether I should have handled it differently. So, was I right to call her out? Yes, because she was littering, and there were trash cans available. It's important to maintain a clean environment to prevent pests and keep the area pleasant for everyone. Was I wrong in how I confronted her? Maybe. I could have been more polite and understanding. Instead of reacting impulsively, I could have calmly explained why it's important to use the trash cans and perhaps educate her on proper waste disposal. In conclusion, while the intent to correct her behavior was right, the approach could have been more considerate and less confrontational. It's a balance between addressing the issue and maintaining a respectful and supportive environment, especially with someone who might be new or sensitive to feedback.
